title: Comparing Buddy Petit and Rene, trumpet rivals at the Eli and Lauderdale
summary: Alexis compares Petit with Rene, names trumpet players around Iberville, and recalls playing for Beans with Black Benny and Willie Humphrey.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Better than Rene for ragtime? Oh no, no. He wasn't. They were... I mean they both had top notch bands. Uh huh. Rene was a high note man, just like I was. High note. They talk that every day right now in the city. They talk that by Mueller's ball, I'll bum every day right now. Uh huh. That's Rene and Ivy. Now I ain't live trumpet players on the order. Now I'm Perez playing next door to me on Iverville, between Burgundy and Ramport, back in the the Lauderdale Theater. Red Happen was playing with Jordan Overshirt and the Lauderdale. And he was playing at the Black and Tan. I'm playing for Beans, see, at the Eli. Beans, Black Benny, Willie Humphrey, Adolp de Cornshed. Black Benny, Willie, Adolp de Cornshed.
Willie Humphrey, I'll talk to Corsier.

And he could hear me playing over there and he'd tell Willie Humphrey, he'd tell the fellow, come down and say, he's going to bust a vessel in his neck. You see Willie Humphrey, anytime you meet him, just ask him that word. Him and I and Black Benny work together. Years, that he liked.
